questions.q: Describe the pathway of the reflex arc when a finger touches a hot object. Portal response box.
questions.a: Heat is the stimulus (1); receptor in the skin (1); impulse along sensory neurone (1); relay neurone in spinal cord via synapses (1); motor neurone (1); effector muscle contracts, finger withdrawn (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes the first line: 'The stimulus is heat, detected by receptors in the skin.'

questions.q: Ruler-drop reaction test at home with an adult: catch a dropped ruler 5 times; record cm and calculate the mean. Is this a reflex?
questions.a: Mean distance recorded (1); not a reflex: it uses the brain and conscious decision (1)
Nervous: electrical impulses, fast, short-lived, precise; hormonal: chemicals in blood, slower, longer-lasting, widespread

questions.q: Explain why a reflex is faster than a conscious response.
questions.a: The impulse passes through the spinal cord via a relay neurone (1), not through the conscious part of the brain, so fewer synapses and no decision time (1)
questions.model: Where does a conscious response go? To the brain to decide. A reflex goes through the spinal cord only. Shorter route, no thinking: faster.

questions.q: How does an impulse cross a synapse?
questions.a: A neurotransmitter diffuses across the gap

questions.q: Name the coordinator in the nervous system.
questions.a: The central nervous system (brain and spinal cord)
